subject: Sentinel Health - compliance bundle pricing and HSM cost split
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@sentinelhealth.com>, procurement@sentinelhealth.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-15 09:12 -0800
Subject: Sentinel Health - compliance bundle pricing and HSM cost split

Hi Alex / Sentinel procurement,

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation I wanted to put three concrete options on the table for the compliance/security bundle (audit logs, KMS/HSM seats, and data residency) so your procurement team has numbers to evaluate. Attached is a first-pass price_workback_v1.xlsx to show unit math. High-level: 

- Option A (Balanced): Audit logs retained 90 days (per-call billing), 1 HSM seat reserved for peak, US residency. Estimated run-rate: $55k/mo.
- Option B (Residency-heavy): 365-day audit retention + dedicated HSM cluster (2 seats). Estimated run-rate: $89k/mo.
- Option C (Pilot): 90-day retention, 1 HSM seat, 3-month pilot at 40% credits on add-ons (apply only to compliance line items). Estimated pilot cost: $21k/mo effective.

Open questions we flagged that will materially change the numbers: HSM seat amortization (seat vs. per-call), exact audit retention window, and whether you want a hybrid residency (partial EU/US). If procurement can share the expected monthly token volume and 95th percentile call concurrency we can firm up the HSM sizing and provide a worked example of amortized seat vs per-call.

Next steps we propose:
- You confirm which option to model and share any token/concurrency estimates.
- We return a revised price_workback and a SOW draft (if you want to run authority-to-sign).

Attaching: price_workback_v1.xlsx (unit math).

If helpful, Lauren can propose a credit split model for HSM that splits capital vs. usage costs. Marissa will own commercial terms.

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0187
redwoodinference.com
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@sentinelhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@sentinelhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-16 10:04 -0800
Subject: Re: Sentinel Health - compliance bundle pricing and HSM cost split

Jonas — thanks for the breakdown, this is helpful. A few questions from procurement and engineering before we escalate to legal: 

1) HSM cost split: our CFO wants to avoid capitalizing the full seat under platform; can you model a 70/30 split (70% of the HSM premium mapped to the regulated product P&L, 30% to platform ops)? If you can show what that looks like in Option A vs Option B we can present to finance.
2) Audit log retention: can retention be tiered (90 / 180 / 365) with a per-GB price that steps down at each threshold? That would probably be our preferred way to optimize costs while keeping compliance.
3) Pilot: procurement is supportive of a pilot but needs clarity on whether the 40% credit applies to one-time onboarding fees or recurring HSM seats as well.

Attached: procurement_questionnaire.xlsx — mostly standard. Can you return a revised workbook and SOW that maps to our 70/30 ask and clarifies credit applicability?

We also need a short SOC2 summary for our security review. Can you attach that?

—Alex
Alex Gomez
Head of Platform Partnerships | Sentinel Health
alex.gomez@sentinelhealth.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@sentinelhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-17 14:23 -0800
Subject: Re: Sentinel Health - compliance bundle pricing and HSM cost split

Alex — great questions, thanks. I discussed this with finance and product; attached are: SOW_draft_v2.pdf and price_workback_v2.xlsx which include a worked example for the 70/30 HSM split and a three-tier audit retention schedule (90/180/365) with step-down per-GB pricing. Notes below: 

- HSM amortization: We show two scenarios in tab 'HSM_split' — (A) seat-amortized over 36 months with 70/30 allocation; (B) hybrid amortized seat + per-call surcharge for burst. For your volume band the hybrid ends up ~8% lower year-1 cost vs pure seat.
- Audit retention: three tiers with clear per-GB pricing. The step-down kicks in at 10TB and 50TB thresholds.
- Pilot credits: To be clear — the 40% pilot credit applies to recurring compliance add-ons (audit storage and HSM seat charge) for the 3-month pilot only; onboarding fee and professional services are excluded. We called this out in SOW_draft_v2, section 2.3.

Marissa — can you confirm commercial language for the 70/30 allocation (is that a discount line or an invoice mapping note)?

Karthik — tagging you to confirm the HSM scaling assumptions and whether a single-seat pilot will cover 95th percentile for their expected concurrency (Alex, if you can share anticipated p95 concurrency we’ll confirm).

Attachments: SOW_draft_v2.pdf, price_workback_v2.xlsx

Thanks —
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@sentinelhealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18 11:08 -0800
Subject: Re: Sentinel Health - compliance bundle pricing and HSM cost split

Alex / team — quick technical note on HSM sizing and cost behavior so procurement has clarity: 

- A single dedicated HSM seat provides a fixed pool of cryptographic ops and key management throughput. For predictable low-concurrency workloads it is most cost effective when amortized as a seat. For spiky workloads a hybrid model (1 seat + per-call burst surcharge) avoids over-provisioning while bounding tail latency.
- In our worked examples I assumed average concurrency 80–120 calls/min and p95 bursts to 320 calls/min. If your p95 is substantially >500 calls/min we’d recommend moving to a 2-seat baseline.
- Operational note: HSM seats can be moved between regions with a 48–72 hour planning window, but data residency guarantees (primary region) require replication.

Commercial suggestion: If Sentinel is willing to commit to a 12-month minimum, we can offer (i) a 25% amortized seat credit for year-1 (applied to the regulated product P&L allocation line) or (ii) a deeper 40% credit if you commit to 36 months. That gives you runway to avoid a large up-front seat cost while protecting our capacity planning.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk the SOW sections and the HSM tab in price_workback_v2.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@sentinelhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@sentinelhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-20 15:40 -0800
Subject: Re: Sentinel Health - compliance bundle pricing and HSM cost split

Jonas / Karthik — appreciate the fast turnaround and the two scenarios. Procurement and finance are aligned enough to move forward with the pilot path:

- We accept the 3-month pilot with 40% credit on recurring compliance add-ons (audit storage + HSM seat) as documented.
- Sentinel will provide p95 concurrency numbers by tomorrow EOD so you can confirm single-seat sizing.
- Please send the updated SOW with the 70/30 allocation language as an invoice mapping note (not a discount line) and a DocuSign-ready agreement. Procurement will need the SOC2 summary — can you attach SOC2_summary.pdf to the DocuSign packet?

If you can get the DocuSign link by Tuesday we’ll start internal approvals.

Next steps: Jonas to share DocuSign link + final SOW; Karthik to confirm sizing once we send p95.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth pilot.

—Alex
